exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.form_cue: Draw the chin straight back into a double chin. Hold 5 sec. Do these before every gym session as part of your warm-up too.
exercises.why: Still your most important exercise. As loads increase, keeping the C6 nerve root decompressed is what protects you.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Flexion
exercises.form_cue: Press forehead into palm and resist. Increase the force slightly vs Phase 1. Hold 8 sec.
exercises.why: Progressive overload for the deep neck flexors so the cervical spine keeps pace with your growing gym strength.

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Extension
exercises.form_cue: Press the back of the head into the palm and resist. Slightly more force than Phase 1. Hold 8 sec.
exercises.why: Builds posterior cervical endurance to support your head under bench presses, rows and squats.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.form_cue: Hold a light band at shoulder height, arms straight. Pull it apart to your chest, squeezing the shoulder blades. Keep the neck relaxed.
exercises.why: Adds light dynamic load to the postural muscles, reinforcing the upright position you'll hold under the bar.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Gentle tilt away from the tight side, focus LEFT. Stop with any radiating symptoms.
exercises.why: Keeps the left-sided tension in check as training volume rises.

exercises.name: Heavy-Slow Wrist Extension
exercises.form_cue: Forearm supported, palm down, holding a dumbbell. Lift the wrist up over 3 sec, lower over 3 sec — both directions slow and loaded. Add weight when 10 reps feel easy.
exercises.why: Heavy-slow resistance is the most effective tendinopathy protocol once pain is low. You now load through the lift, not just the lower.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.form_cue: Forearm on thigh or bench, palm down, light dumbbell. Curl the wrist up, control it down. Smooth tempo.
exercises.why: Builds extensor strength and endurance — the muscles that the C6 nerve once compromised. Restoring them protects the elbow during pulls.

exercises.name: Loaded Supination / Pronation
exercises.form_cue: Hold a dumbbell by one end, elbow at your side. Rotate palm-up to palm-down slowly. Increase the offset weight gradually.
exercises.why: Progressively loads the forearm rotators that stabilise the lateral epicondyle under grip-heavy gym work.

exercises.name: Grip Squeezes
exercises.form_cue: Squeeze a gripper or soft ball, hold 3 sec, release. Should be pain-free — back off the resistance if not.
exercises.why: Rebuilds the grip you'll need for rows and carries. Pain-free grip work drives blood flow and tendon healing.

exercises.name: Barbell Box Squat (or Goblet Squat)
exercises.form_cue: Bar on the upper back, brace, sit back to the box, drive up. Eyes forward, neck neutral — never look up. If the bar bothers your neck, keep loading the goblet squat.
exercises.why: Your first real barbell pattern. The box controls depth and the neutral-neck cues keep your cervical spine out of trouble while you build serious leg strength.

exercises.name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
exercises.form_cue: Stand inside the trap bar, hinge, grab the neutral handles, push the floor away. Flat back, neutral neck, chest proud. Straps OK to spare the elbow.
exercises.why: The trap bar keeps the load beside you rather than in front, dramatically reducing spinal and neck stress versus a straight-bar deadlift — ideal for your back.

exercises.name: Single-Arm DB Row
exercises.form_cue: One hand and knee on a bench, flat back, head in line with your spine (don't crane it up). Row the dumbbell to your hip.
exercises.why: Builds unilateral back strength and irons out left/right imbalances. The supported position keeps the neck safe.

exercises.name: DB Incline Press
exercises.form_cue: Bench at ~30°. Press dumbbells up and slightly together. Keep shoulder blades pinned, neck relaxed against the pad.
exercises.why: An incline is gentler on the shoulder than a flat bench and keeps the neck supported while you build pressing strength.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.form_cue: Press the end of a barbell up and away at an angle, one arm at a time. Stand tall, ribs down.
exercises.why: Your overhead substitute. It trains vertical pressing strength WITHOUT the neck-craning and compression of a strict overhead press — perfect while your cervical spine earns that movement back.

exercises.name: DB Split Squat
exercises.form_cue: Dumbbells at your sides, one foot forward. Drop the back knee straight down, drive through the front heel. Tall chest.
exercises.why: Single-leg strength and balance that carries directly into running and protects the knees.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.form_cue: Stand sideways to a cable/band at chest height. Press straight out and resist the pull to rotate. Brace hard.
exercises.why: Anti-rotation core strength stabilises your trunk under load and is critical for an efficient running stride.
